title: Ruling on Review Timing and Long-Term Hardship Hold Extensions
content:
## Ruling

Under Hardship and Protective Holds, the anchor of a long-term extension of a Long-Term Hardship Hold depends on the status review that next falls due after the hold's current end date. Reviews of this tier fall due every review interval of 60 calendar days counted from the hold's start date, and a review falling due on the current end date itself counts as one inside the hold. The review overdue days of the tier are 15 calendar days.

1. Where that review falls due no more than 15 days after the current end date and every review that has fallen due by today was recorded as continuing the hold, the extension is counted from the last day of that review's overdue window, adding the days from the current end date to that review's due date plus the 15 review overdue days.
2. Where that review falls due within the same period but fewer reviews were recorded as continuing the hold than have fallen due, the extension is counted from that review's due date, adding the days from the current end date to that due date.
3. Otherwise the extension is counted from the day after the current end date and adds nothing.

"Fallen due by today" includes a review whose due date is today. The comparison is between the number of reviews in the hold's history recorded as continuing the hold and the number of reviews that have fallen due by today.

## Dated example (hypothetical)

Start date 1 March. Reviews fall due on 30 April, 29 June and 28 August.

| Current end date | Next review after it | Days from the end date to that review | Continuing reviews against reviews fallen due (today 10 August: 2 fallen due) | Days added on this ground |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 27 August | 28 August | 1 | 2 recorded as continuing | 1 plus 15, that is 16 — counted from 12 September |
| 27 August | 28 August | 1 | 1 recorded as continuing | 1 — counted from 28 August |
| 10 August | 28 August | 18 | any | Nothing — more than 15 days |

## Boundary points

- A review falling due exactly 15 days after the current end date is "no more than 15 days" after it; one falling due 16 days after is not.
- If the current end date is itself a review due date (say 29 June), that review counts inside the hold; the next review is the following one, 60 days later, which is more than 15 days away, so nothing is added.
